a similar situation. In addition, the episode of binge eating must
be characterized by the subject sensing a lack of control (e.g., 
the subject feels he or she cannot stop or control what or how 
much he or she is eating).110 When deﬁ ning a binge, it is impor-
tant to consider the context in which the food is consumed. For
example, normal food consumption during a holiday or celebra-
tion might be considered excessive during a typical meal. Foods
consumed during a binge are often those that are sweet and 
kcal-rich, such as ice cream or cake.
Th e American Psychiatric Association recognizes two mutu-
ally exclusive subtypes of BN: purging and nonpurging. In the 
purging subtype, the patient regularly engages in some type of 
purging behavior such as self-induced vomiting or the misuse
of laxatives, diuretics, or enemas. Th e most common form 
of purging is self-induced vomiting, which is used by 80% to 
90% of persons treated for BN
